correctness.rationale: PASS: In the finite n-point contranominal context gIm iff g!=m, derivation is set complementation and all object extents are closed. Min_P(X) is an antichain; choosing X equal to an arbitrary antichain produces every antichain, so typical extents recover precisely the undirected comparability graph. For antecedent A=G\X, the nonclassical singleton consequents are X\Min_P(X). The contribution from x is the generating difference z((1+z)^(n-1)-(1+z)^(n-1-d_P(x))), yielding the displayed H_P and inversion by powers of 1+z. For X={x,y}, the premise G\{x,y} preferentially entails y exactly when x is strictly preferred to y, so n-2 premises recover P. For n>=3, make all z in nonempty Z below y, and optionally x below y; all X of size>=3 have identical minima, proving sharpness even for set-valued conclusions. Transitive closures of the explicit 5-point P and Q relations give identical labeled comparability graph, predecessor multiset {0,0,1,2,3}, and H=6z^2+14z^3+11z^4+3z^5 but nonisomorphic Hasse cover orientation. Independent direct subset enumeration confirmed the two 3-point forks and the two 5-point spectra, not used as all-n proof. Range n>=2 and all finite posets.

value.rationale: PASS: The motivating FCA literature examines what typical concepts capture compared with preferential attribute conditionals. This supplies a canonical complete information hierarchy rather than a renamed count: a typical-antichain family forgets orientations, H_P recovers just predecessor-count multiplicities, and n-2 premise conditional tables recover all strict comparisons, with explicit sharp counterexamples. These are exact information limitations useful for preferential knowledge representation even without generalising to arbitrary formal contexts.
